corrections.reason: The pre-registered rubric defines D5 as levels that are 'not monotonically ordered' or 'not mutually distinguishable situations'. weak/okay/strong/excellent are ordered and distinguishable, so they do not meet the rubric text. The original label applied the docs' style guidance ('levels must describe concrete situations') instead of the rubric. Rubric fidelity wins. The corresponding lint rule score/bare-levels was demoted warn -> info for the same reason.
